newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-U.S. Sept consumer spending seen soft.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-U.S. Sept consumer spending seen soft.

text.p: Despite an increase in wages, U.S. consumers have elected to put the brakes on spending, opting instead to save for a rainy day, experts said.
"The consumer is not rushing out to spend its increased income and the savings rate continues to rise," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securites Inc.
"So you tend to have some pent up spending that's going to take place ... it's just a matter of time," he added.
U.S. experts predict a 0.6-percent gain in personal income for September after the Labor Department reported a six-cent gain in hourly earnings in September's employment report.
The Commerce Department will report personal income and spending in September at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday, November 1.
Soft retail sales last month are expected to pressure consumption to a 0.3-percent rise level for September, down from a 0.6-percent increase in August.
Best predicted, however, that an acceleration in consumption will occur going into the end of year, and he noted an accumulation in savings.
"The savings rate continues to rise and consumption has been relatively soft, but this trend should reverse as we head into the end of the year," Best said.
Healthy holiday sales also are expected to boost consumption going forward, he added.
Best forecasted a 0.5-percent gain in personal income and a modest 0.1-percent rise in consumption last month.
Meanwhile, economists said Wednesday's release of third quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by the Commerce Department shed some light on Thursday's consumption figure.
Commerce, in its first estimate of third quarter GDP, reported spending up 0.4 percent, sharply lower then the second quarter's final reading of 3.4 percent.
"This number is going to be considered old news as it comes after Wednesday's third quarter GDP report," said Michelle Colley Laughlin, Treasury market strategist at Prudential Securities Inc.
"Although people look at the pace of income and the savings rate, the number's not going to have a lot of weight in the context of more important economic data this week," Laughlin added.
The Prudential strategist predicted a 0.7-percent increase in September personal income, in line with the gain in hourly earnings reported in the September's jobs report.
Laughlin expects consumption to show a modest gain of 0.3 percent.

"Income is going to show a good growth rate in September and consumption is going to be stagnant ... that means the savings rate for the month will be high," said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets.
"Basically, (spending) continued along the trend of the third quarter, which was a much weaker consumption trend," Kretzmer added.
Mediocre department store sales and a 5.0-percent drop in September vehicle sales are expected to depress September consumption, Kretzmer added.
However, he said he expected a strong 0.8-percent gain in personal income following the hourly wage increase in the September employment report.
"My guess is the fourth quarter will be a little stronger than the third quarter in terms of consumption, but still not above trend, which I see somewhere around 2.0 percent," Kretzmer added.
Despite robust income growth in the last few months, Kretzmer predicted a slowing in income growth in the months ahead in response to slower growth in the economy.
